blindness.agent_reported_external_sources:
Not none. Three things came from outside docs/:

1. Prior knowledge of the `console` crate (which docs/index.md and the styling
   docs name as the layer underneath standout's styles): its `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1`
   environment variable is what actually makes ANSI survive a pipe. I set it
   in-process in `src/styling.rs`. Nothing in docs/ mentions it; I found the
   need for it empirically (`--output=term` piped emitted no ANSI) and reached
   for `CLICOLOR_FORCE` from memory, then confirmed it by running the binary.
2. Prior knowledge of Jinja/MiniJinja filter semantics — `map(attribute=...)`,
   `map("length")`, `max`, `loop.first`, and `{%-`/`-%}` whitespace control —
   for the width computation in the template. docs/ links to the MiniJinja docs
   but I did not open them; I wrote the expressions from memory and verified
   them by running the binary.
3. Prior knowledge of `std::io::IsTerminal` and `std::process` for the pager
   subprocess; ordinary Rust standard-library knowledge, no standout involved.

No web search, no repository or crate source consulted. I did read `rustc`
diagnostics that quote standout's own signatures (for example the
`GroupBuilder::command` bound printed from `standout-8.1.1/src/cli/group.rs`,
and the `#[dispatch(...)]` macro's "expected one of:" attribute list); those
came from building, not from opening the crate's files.

answers.docs.gaps:
1. docs/topics/output-modes.md, "Term vs Text": "**Term**: Always applies ANSI
   escape codes, even when piping: `myapp list --output=term > colored.txt`".
   It does not. `systemdlike --output term | cat -v` produced no escape codes
   at all; the same command with `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` in the environment produced
   `^[[1mUNIT ... ^[[0m`. The colors_supported() check the same doc describes
   for Auto mode appears to gate Term as well, so "always" is wrong unless the
   underlying terminal abstraction is separately told to force color.

2. docs/topics/app-configuration.md, "With Configuration":
   `.command_with("delete", delete_handler, |cfg| cfg.template_name("delete"))`.
   `template_name` does not exist on `CommandConfig` in 8.1.1; the method is
   `template`. The same doc's "Basic Setup" block uses `config.template_name("list")`
   too, so the error is repeated.

3. The `#[dispatch(...)]` attribute list is never documented as a whole (the
   macro itself knows sixteen attributes), and `pure` — required whenever the
   handler is written with `#[handler]`'s typed signature — is used in examples
   without a word of explanation. docs/guides/intro-to-standout.md §7.2.1 shows
   the same setup *without* `pure`, which does not compile.

4. Nothing documents how `#[handler]` maps a parameter name to a Clap argument
   id. It kebab-cases (`no_legend` -> `no-legend`), which silently disagrees
   with Clap's derive (`no_legend`) and fails as a runtime panic. The
   "Parameter Annotations" table in docs/crates/dispatch/topics/handler-contract.md
   shows `matches.get_flag("name")`, implying the parameter name is used
   verbatim.

5. Nothing documents whether rendered output is newline-terminated by the
   framework. It appends one without trimming, which is observable behavior
   templates have to be written around.

6. Two capabilities the spec asks for have no framework support and no
   documentation: an environment-driven color policy (`NO_COLOR` and an
   app-specific override) and paging of ordinary command output. Paging is
   documented only for help topics — docs/topics/topics-system.md, "Standout
   tries pagers in order: 1. `$PAGER` environment variable" — and
   docs/topics/execution-outcomes.md is explicit that `run()` pages only
   `SuccessKind::PagedHelp`. Both had to be built in the application.
answers.friction:
1. `#[derive(Dispatch)]` names commands in snake_case while Clap's derive names
   subcommands in kebab-case, and nothing bridges the two. Variant `ListUnits`
   plus `#[dispatch(default)]` produced, for a naked invocation:

       error: unrecognized subcommand 'list_units'
         tip: a similar subcommand exists: 'list-units'

   and an explicit `systemdlike list-units` printed nothing at all (a silent
   `NoMatch`, since `run`'s `false` return is easy to ignore). There is no
   per-variant rename:

       error: unknown attribute, expected one of: handler, template,
       pre_dispatch, post_dispatch, post_output, questionnaire, nested, skip,
       default, list_view, item_type, pipe_to, pipe_through, pipe_to_clipboard,
       simple, pure

   I dropped the derive and registered through the builder instead.

2. The `#[handler]` macro derives the argument id by kebab-casing the parameter
   name, but Clap's derive uses the snake_case field name, so the mismatch is a
   runtime panic rather than a compile error:

       thread 'main' panicked at src/main.rs:62:5:
       Mismatch between definition and access of `no-legend`. Unknown argument
       or group id.

   Fixed with `#[flag(name = "no_legend")]`.

3. `#[dispatch(pure)]` is used in docs/index.md and
   docs/guides/minimal-single-crate.md, omitted in
   docs/guides/intro-to-standout.md §7.2.1, and explained nowhere. Omitting it
   fails to compile:

       error[E0631]: type mismatch in function arguments
       = note: expected function signature `for<'a, 'b> fn(&'a ArgMatches, &'b CommandContext) -> _`
                  found function signature `fn(std::option::Option<std::string::String>, bool) -> _`

4. docs/topics/app-configuration.md says
   `.command_with("delete", delete_handler, |cfg| cfg.template_name("delete"))`,
   but in 8.1.1:

       error[E0599]: no method named `template_name` found for struct `CommandConfig<H>`
       help: there is a method `template` with a similar name

5. `--output=term` does not force ANSI through a pipe (see the docs gap below);
   I had to discover `CLICOLOR_FORCE` to satisfy the spec's rules 1 and 2.

6. There is no documented way to set the output mode programmatically, so the
   color decision has to be expressed as an argument. `AppBuilder::output_mode`
   exists but is a getter:

       error[E0061]: this method takes 0 arguments but 1 argument was supplied
       95 |     let _probe = App::builder().output_mode(standout::OutputMode::Term);

   And appending my own `--output` next to a user's is refused:

       error: the argument '--output <MODE>' cannot be used multiple times

   so `src/styling.rs` strips any user-supplied `--output` before appending the
   decided one.

7. Rendered text gets a newline appended without the trailing newline being
   trimmed first, so a template ending in a newline yields a stray blank line.
   `--no-legend` printed an extra empty line until I moved to emitting each
   row's newline *before* the row (`{% if legend or not loop.first %}`).

answers.summary:
Built `systemdlike` in `app/`: a standout 8.1.1 CLI over the frozen four-row
unit table. `cargo build`, `cargo build --release` and `cargo test` (12 tests)
all pass, and I verified the binary by hand, including under a PTY (`script -q
/dev/null ...`) for the terminal-attended paths.

Shape:
- `src/units.rs` — CLI-free core: the frozen table, listing order, `--state`
  filtering. Unit tested.
- `src/main.rs` — Clap definition (`list-units` plus `--state`, `--no-legend`,
  `--plain`, `--no-pager`), a `#[handler]` adapter returning the `UnitsView`
  DTO, and `App::builder()` wiring with `.default_command("list-units")` so the
  naked line is `list-units`, flags included.
- `src/templates/list-units.jinja` — the whole layout: column widths taken from
  the rendered rows (header included only when shown), `col` padding on every
  column but the last, header row and `<N> units listed.` legend.
- `src/styles/default.css` — bold header, green `active`, yellow `inactive`.
- `src/styling.rs` — the color rule cascade, expressed as the `--output` mode
  handed to the framework.
- `src/pager.rs` — the pager rule cascade and the paging subprocess.

Verified against SPEC.md: default output and `--state active` output are
byte-identical to the two blocks in the spec; `--no-legend` leaves only data
rows with no stray blank line; `--plain` piped is byte-identical to default
piped; paged output (`PAGER=cat`) is byte-identical to `--no-pager` output; all
16 cells of the color matrix (piped/tty x default/`--plain`/`--output
term|text`/`SYSTEMDLIKE_COLORS=0|1`/`NO_COLOR`, including
`SYSTEMDLIKE_COLORS=1` under `NO_COLOR` and piped) behave as specified; exit 0
for success and help, exit 2 for a bad `--state` value, an unknown flag, and an
unknown subcommand.
answers.workarounds:
All are in the CLI layer, none in the core or the handler:

1. `src/styling.rs` decides color and hands the decision to the framework by
   rewriting argv: it strips any user-supplied `--output` and appends
   `--output=term` or `--output=text`. This is the workaround for there being
   no builder-side output mode.
2. Same file: `std::env::set_var("CLICOLOR_FORCE", "1")` before running,
   whenever ANSI is forced. Without it `--output=term` renders plain through a
   pipe, so rules 1 and 2 of the spec's color discipline cannot be met.
3. Because the color and pager decisions are needed before Clap parses, they
   are made by scanning argv directly for `--plain`, `--no-pager`,
   `--output`, and `--output-file-path` rather than reading `ArgMatches`. The
   flags are still declared on the Clap command, so `--help` and usage errors
   stay honest; the scan is only a pre-read.
4. `src/main.rs` uses `run_to_string` plus its own pager subprocess and exit
   code when paging, because `run()` owns the final write and pages help only.
   The non-paging path still uses `run()`, so the framework owns the common
   case. I checked the two paths are byte-identical (`PAGER=cat` vs
   `--no-pager` under a PTY).
5. `#[derive(Dispatch)]` is not used; the command is registered with
   `.command_with("list-units", handlers::list_units__handler, ...)`, naming the
   function the `#[handler]` macro generates, because the derive would register
   the command as `list_units`.
6. `#[flag(name = "no_legend")]` spells the Clap argument id explicitly to
   defeat the macro's kebab-casing.

The `--output-file-path` guard in `src/pager.rs` is a deliberate small
decision, not a workaround: an invocation redirected to a file is not paged.
